subject: Control Variables in Mediation models with Lavaan

messages.author: 47b309570fab387c
messages.subject: Control Variables in Mediation models with Lavaan
parts:
I'm running a mediation analysis with the Index of participation on digital platform as the outcome, Frequency of information on social media as predictor and Frequency of discussion on social media as mediator. I’m using lavaan in R. I have data from 3 time points and i want to estimate the direct impact of information on social media in wave 1 on the index of participation measured in wave 3, mediated by the frequency of discussion on social media in wave 2. I also want to control such associations by a bunch of control variables, namely gender, age, ideology, political interest and economic uncertainty. Does the code look right? I’m not exactly sure if I can include in the mediation model the control variables and, if so, I can have to include them only in the outcome model or also in mediation model, as the control variables may have an impact both in participation and discussion in social media.

Participation_socialmedia <- ' 
# outcome model 
           Digital_3  ~   c1* Infosocialmedia_1 + b1*Discussionsocial_2 +   Left_1 + Center_1 + Right_1  + Edulevel_1 + Gender_1 + Polint_1 + Economicunc_1
            # mediator models
       Discussionsocial_2 ~ a1* Infosocialmedia_1 + Infonews_1 +  Infotv_1 +  Inforadio_1  +  Left_1 + Center_1 + Right_1 + Edulevel_1 + Gender_1 + Polint_1 + Economicunc_1

# indirect effects (IDE)
  medVar1IDE  := a1*b1
 # Direct effects
  direct:= c1
 
# total effect
total := c1 + (a1*b1) 
'

Model_socialmedia <- sem(Participation_socialmedia, data=data, meanstructure=TRUE, se="bootstrap", bootstrap=500)
summary(Model_socialmedia, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

Many thanks in advance for your feedback!!!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Control Variables in Mediation models with Lavaan
parts:
If you want your a and b (and c) paths to have the same interpretation (i.e., with respect to "controlling for ..."), I recommend estimating the same covariate effects on both the mediator(s) and outcome(s).  That way the interpretation of the indirect effect is also straight-forward with respect to the control variables.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
